turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good morning, Mr. Tan. I'm Dr. Kumar, the anesthesiologist who'll be taking care of you during your surgery today. I just want to go over a few things to make sure we're all set for your laparoscopic cholecystectomy under general anesthesia with an LMA.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Good morning, doctor. I'm ready, just want to get this done and feel better.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Great. Can you tell me a bit about your medical history and how you've been feeling lately?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Sure. I've had gallstones for a while now, and the doctor said surgery is the best way to go. I also have high blood pressure, diabetes, and my BMI is a bit high. Oh, and my kidney function is a little off, but it's stable.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thank you. Let's go through your medications. I see here that you're on Metformin, Lisinopril, Atorvastatin, Insulin Glargine, and Ranitidine. Can you confirm if you're still taking all of these, or have any been changed or stopped?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Most of them are still the same, doctor. I take Metformin 500mg twice a day, Lisinopril 10mg once a day, Atorvastatin 20mg once a day, and Insulin Glargine 30 units once at night. But I stopped the Ranitidine about six months ago because the doctor said my peptic ulcer had healed and I didn't need it anymore.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thanks for clarifying that. It's important we have the most up-to-date medication list. Do you have any allergies? I see penicillin listed with a rash.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes, I had a rash when I took penicillin before, so I avoid that. No other drug allergies that I know of.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good. Have you had any previous surgeries or anesthesia? Any issues like waking up during surgery, difficult intubation, or nausea afterward?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, this is my first surgery. I've never had anesthesia before, so I'm a bit nervous about that.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: That's completely normal. We'll make sure you're comfortable and safe throughout. Are you NPO since midnight? Nothing by mouth after 8 PM?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes, I haven't had anything to eat or drink since last night. Just a sip of water with my morning insulin, but that was hours ago.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Perfect. And how would you describe your overall energy level and ability to perform daily activities?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I can still walk and do my daily tasks, but I do get a bit tired, especially after meals. But I manage okay lah.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thanks for that information. We'll make sure to tailor your anesthesia plan to your needs. You'll be asleep during the surgery, and we'll use a laryngeal mask airway to help you breathe. You'll have a tube in your throat only if needed, but we'll try to avoid that if possible.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Alright, that sounds good. I trust you, doctor.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thank you, Mr. Tan. We'll be with you every step of the way. I'll see you in the operating room shortly. Any last questions?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, I think that's all. Thank you for explaining everything so clearly.
